title: A memoising cache that does not leak
description:
Write `memoize(fn)` that returns a function remembering `fn`'s result for each **table** argument it has been called with. The memory is a table with weak keys, so arguments that are no longer used elsewhere are forgotten. The returned function also counts how often `fn` itself was really called, available as `calls()` on a second return value.

```lua
local area, stats = memoize(function(r) return r.w * r.h end)
local box = { w = 3, h = 4 }
area(box); area(box)
print(stats.calls())       --> 1
```

solution.solution.lua:
function memoize(fn)
    local results = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
    local calls = 0
    local function cached(arg)
        local value = results[arg]
        if value == nil then
            calls = calls + 1
            value = fn(arg)
            results[arg] = value
        end
        return value
    end
    local stats = {
        calls = function() return calls end,
        size = function()
            local n = 0
            for _ in pairs(results) do n = n + 1 end
            return n
        end,
    }
    return cached, stats
end

hints: `setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })` is the whole trick: entries whose key table is used nowhere else vanish at the next collection.
The tests also call `stats.size()`, which counts the entries still in the cache: return it next to `calls`.
unitTests:
test("remembers", function()
    local area, stats = memoize(function(r) return r.w * r.h end)
    local box = { w = 3, h = 4 }
    check_eq(area(box), 12)
    check_eq(area(box), 12)
    check_eq(stats.calls(), 1)
    check_eq(area({ w = 1, h = 1 }), 1)
    check_eq(stats.calls(), 2)
end)

test("forgets unused arguments", function()
    local f, stats = memoize(function(t) return #t end)
    local keep = { 1, 2, 3 }
    f(keep)
    for i = 1, 100 do f({ i }) end
    collectgarbage()
    collectgarbage()
    check_eq(stats.size(), 1)
    check_eq(f(keep), 3)
    check_eq(stats.calls(), 101)
end)
